sections.title: The people building the AI factories.
sections.intro: Construction spending, recruitment demand and training are separate signals. These U.S. series cover data centers generally; they do not measure net jobs created by AI.

cards.title: Recruitment demand
cards.body: Indeed reports that data-center postings more than doubled over two years. Keyword matching can miss relevant roles and include unrelated jobs. Its installation/maintenance pay comparison is occupation- and study-specific, not a national electrician wage increase.
cards.gap: A downloadable DC electrician child series and exact intermediate index values were not verified. Missing values are not zero.

cards.title: Electrical training ALLIANCE
cards.body: Google supports etA, created by IBEW and NECA, to expand electrical training. Curriculum includes AI tools alongside trade skills. Apprentice targets are separate from training existing electrical workers.
cards.gap: Actual cohort enrollment, completion and job-placement counts require program reporting.

cards.title: America’s Workforce Academy
cards.body: Meta announced pilots in Louisiana, Ohio, Indiana and Texas. An August update reports the first graduating cohort. Its graduate job guarantee is a promise; no aggregate verified placement count is recorded here.
cards.gap: Separate promised jobs, graduates and verified placements. Applications are not training seats.

cards.title: Jeffersonville, Indiana · Turner
cards.body: Turner identifies itself as the builder selected for Meta’s Jeffersonville campus. Its announcement describes prefabricated assemblies and anticipated construction work. This establishes the contractor relationship, not current completion.
cards.gap: Current commissioning, subcontractor roster and actual site payroll need newer primary evidence.

cards.title: Richland Parish, Louisiana · Mortenson
cards.body: Mortenson identifies site preparation, underground utilities, medium-voltage distribution and substations, water and wastewater facilities, and outside-plant fiber in its scope. These trades connect construction investment to a usable AI factory.
cards.gap: The project page has no verified publication date. Peak and expected jobs are not actual permanent hires.

sections.title: Different routes to firm clean power.
sections.intro: A restart can restore generation, a fleet PPA contracts existing supply, and an SMR agreement supports future construction. Contracted MW cannot be added into new operating generation.

cards.title: Crane · Constellation / Microsoft
cards.body: The September 2024 agreement links a proposed plant restart to Microsoft power matching. The original commercial-operation target was 2028, subject to approvals; see the project tracker for subsequent milestones.
cards.gap: Track regulatory authorization and first delivered generation separately from the PPA.

cards.title: Susquehanna · Talen / Amazon
cards.body: Talen’s filed agreement contracts existing nuclear output. Separate discussions about uprates and small reactors do not establish that additional generation has been built.
cards.gap: Additional measured outcomes remain a research priority.

cards.title: Kairos Power / Google
cards.body: The original agreement targets a first reactor in 2030 and additional deployments through 2035. The displayed quantity is the agreement ceiling; permits, financed construction and commercial output require their own records.
cards.gap: Additional measured outcomes remain a research priority.

sections.title: A finished accelerator needs the whole supply chain.
sections.intro: A U.S.-fabricated logic die is not a finished domestic AI accelerator. HBM, advanced packaging, substrates and test have their own locations and production milestones; Arizona fabrication does not prove Arizona CoWoS output.

cards.title: SK hynix · HBM4
cards.body: SK hynix reported completed development and a prepared mass-production system. This dated milestone does not itself establish shipment volume or every customer’s qualification.
cards.gap: Additional measured outcomes remain a research priority.

cards.title: Samsung · HBM4
cards.body: Samsung reported mass production and commercial shipments to customers. Customer-by-customer qualification and shipped stack counts remain undisclosed in this source.
cards.gap: Additional measured outcomes remain a research priority.

cards.title: Micron · HBM4
cards.body: Micron reported HBM4 high-volume production designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin. Memory production and completed accelerator deployments are different milestones.
cards.gap: Additional measured outcomes remain a research priority.

cards.title: Marvell and the CPO ecosystem
cards.body: Marvell describes optical conversion near the ASIC and reference designs involving SENKO, Jabil and Mikros Technologies. The blog establishes component roles and serviceability concepts; it does not establish fleet deployment or CPO revenue.
cards.gap: Additional measured outcomes remain a research priority.

sections.title: From model responses to completed tasks.
sections.intro: A harness manages the tool loop, permissions, context, memory and execution environment around a model. Product availability and subscription prices do not measure useful work completed. Prices below were checked September 7, 2026; taxes, overages and human review can add cost.

cards.title: Claude Code · Pro
cards.body: Included in Claude Pro at monthly billing. The subscription spans Claude products and has usage limits; it is not a dedicated unlimited coding budget.
cards.gap: Subscription price is not cost per successfully completed task.

cards.title: Cursor Agent / CLI / cloud
cards.body: Individual Pro monthly plan. Agent usage limits and separately metered products apply; editor, CLI and hosted cloud agents are different execution surfaces.
cards.gap: Subscription price is not cost per successfully completed task.

cards.title: GitHub Copilot · Pro
cards.body: Monthly per-user Pro plan includes access to cloud agent and code review. Included credits and additional usage are separate from seat price.
cards.gap: Subscription price is not cost per successfully completed task.

cards.title: Codex CLI
cards.body: ChatGPT Plus monthly plan is one subscription route. Local CLI can also use separately billed API access; local tool execution does not imply a locally hosted model.
cards.gap: Subscription price is not cost per successfully completed task.

cards.title: Codex cloud
cards.body: Cloud tasks run in hosted environments. The same reviewed plan page distinguishes cloud access from API-key CLI access; API-key billing does not include cloud features. This is a separate surface, not another model family.
cards.gap: Additional measured outcomes remain a research priority.

cards.title: Open weights · explicit license scope
cards.body: DeepSeek-R1’s main weights and code use MIT terms; distilled Llama derivatives retain additional upstream conditions. Qwen3-32B uses Apache 2.0. These named checkpoints do not establish licenses for every family member, complete training-data openness or production adoption.
cards.gap: Other model families need checkpoint-specific license review. Downloads are not active enterprise deployments.

cards.title: Gemini CLI
cards.body: Google’s Apache 2.0 CLI offers file and shell tools, MCP connections and checkpointing. Software licensing is distinct from Gemini model access, quotas and billing.
cards.gap: Outcome measurements require independent follow-up.

cards.title: OpenClaw
cards.body: OpenClaw connects models, tools and scheduled work. Stack Ledger’s configured local runtime is shown in the footer; configuration does not establish global adoption or a completed daily run. Model inference, hardware and operations have separate costs.
cards.gap: Outcome measurements require independent follow-up.

sections.title: Useful outcomes, across different kinds of work.
sections.intro: Digital work, physical AI, medicine and science need different evidence. A merged change, paid trip, clinical endpoint and operational forecast are not interchangeable measures of progress.

cards.title: Digital work
cards.body: Coding harnesses can edit files, run tools and prepare changes. The Models page now separates execution surfaces and dated subscriptions. Seats, generated code and product revenue do not establish hours saved or quality-adjusted productivity.
cards.gap: Named enterprise studies need task, comparison, sample, quality and human-oversight costs.

cards.title: Physical AI
cards.stage: See separate autonomy and robotics records
cards.body: Paid robotaxi trips, unsupervised miles and warehouse tasks remain separate datasets. The existing vehicle and robotics cards retain geography, supervision and deployment stage.
cards.gap: Additional measured outcomes remain a research priority.

cards.title: Medicine · Moderna / Merck
cards.body: INTerpath-001 (NCT05933577) compares intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157 / V940) plus pembrolizumab with pembrolizumab alone after melanoma surgery. The randomized, double-blind trial reportedly met recurrence-free and distant-metastasis-free survival endpoints. It is an investigational treatment, not an approval. This release does not isolate an AI contribution to clinical efficacy.
cards.gap: Detailed Phase 3 effect sizes and safety tables await the cited presentation/publication. Earlier KEYNOTE-942 Phase 2b hazard ratios must not be substituted.

cards.title: Science · operational AI weather
cards.body: ECMWF documents operational support for AIFS Single from February 25, 2025 and AIFS ensemble from July 1, 2025. This is a deployed forecasting service, beyond a research-paper demonstration; weather skill and economic benefit still need separate evaluation.
cards.gap: Track version-specific forecast verification, failure modes and user outcomes; initial operational dates do not identify today’s model version.

cards.title: Medicine · Recursion REC-4881
cards.body: The December 2025 TUPELO disclosure reports polyp-burden reduction after treatment in a small evaluable group. The endpoint is a surrogate measure; open-label comparisons do not establish reduced cancer incidence or a benefit attributable specifically to AI.
cards.gap: Track controlled confirmation, adverse events, complete participant disposition, and portfolio discontinuations alongside positive readouts.

cards.title: Medicine · Isomorphic Labs
cards.body: The May 2026 disclosure describes funding to develop its drug-design engine and advance therapeutic programs toward the clinic. It does not identify a molecule-level clinical efficacy result. The molecule and trial stage remain unspecified for this disclosure.
cards.gap: A named asset, registry identifier, phase and results are needed before recording a clinical outcome.

sections.title: Power, with a pre-boom baseline
sections.intro: Historical utility-scale generation and near-term forecasts share a plot with a separately marked, broader national scenario through 2030. The 2028 scope boundary matters: do not infer a comparable growth rate across it.

sections.title: The trades behind the buildout
sections.intro: Five historical electrician-employment estimates put today’s electrical buildout in context. A marked 2021 methodology break limits comparisons; this is not a count of AI-created jobs.

sections.title: Foundry revenue before and during the AI ramp
sections.intro: Seven annual observations cover all TSMC customers and end markets. Revenue is not wafer capacity or domestic value added.

sections.title: Planning beyond 2030
sections.intro: IEA’s 2025 sensitivity cases extend to 2035. Each case stays separate, with its original vintage; the newer headline outlook elsewhere remains unchanged. Government targets through 2050 are a different evidence class.

cards.title: Headwinds
cards.body: A separate sensitivity case for planning power supply. Historical demand and this scenario endpoint are not an interpolated annual path.
cards.gap: Track revised scenario vintages, efficiency assumptions, grid bottlenecks and delivered capacity.

sections.title: More capacity for serious work
sections.intro: Individual premium subscriptions, reviewed September 7, 2026. These buy different product allowances; matching prices or 5x/20x labels do not imply equivalent compute, models or completed work. API usage is billed separately.

cards.title: ChatGPT Pro 5x
cards.body: Five times the Plus Codex allowance in the documented plan comparison. Task size, selected model, speed and weekly limits affect actual usage; API billing is separate.
cards.gap: Track changes to monthly/annual billing, model eligibility, allowance resets, extra usage and regional prices.

cards.body: Twenty times the Plus Codex allowance. The documented unlimited desktop Voice benefit does not make agent tasks unlimited. API billing is separate.

cards.title: Claude Max 5x

cards.gap: Track changes to monthly/annual billing, model eligibility, allowance resets, extra usage and regional prices.

cards.title: Claude Max 20x
cards.body: Twenty times Pro capacity per session in the official individual-plan guide. Model availability, session and weekly limits, and any extra usage charges remain separate.
cards.gap: Track changes to monthly/annual billing, model eligibility, allowance resets, extra usage and regional prices.

cards.title: SuperGrok
cards.body: The current comparison lists Grok 4.6, Grok Bot access, connectors and increased feature limits. A subscription is not an unrestricted API balance.
cards.gap: Track changes to monthly/annual billing, model eligibility, allowance resets, extra usage and regional prices.

cards.title: SuperGrok Plus
cards.body: Adds higher usage across Chat, Imagine, Voice and Build, priority access and 1080p video creation. Product usage and API token charges are different measures.
cards.gap: Track changes to monthly/annual billing, model eligibility, allowance resets, extra usage and regional prices.

cards.title: SuperGrok Heavy
cards.body: Heavy is listed on the official comparison and Bot eligibility pages. The accessible page did not expose its current monthly amount, and the interactive price tab could not be retrieved. Price remains unverified rather than reusing an older reported amount.

sections.title: The frontier, with release status attached
sections.intro: Current models, their predecessors, restricted access and upcoming releases in one research view. Standard API input/output prices are compared separately from subscriptions. Vendor capability claims are not independent rankings.

cards.title: Claude Opus 5
cards.body: Designed for coding and professional work. The launch identifies Opus 5 as an everyday model and describes improved efficiency. Launch-era default-plan claims are not treated as current model entitlements.
cards.gap: Track revised access, prices, independent evaluations, completed-task costs and reliability.

cards.title: Claude Fable 5
cards.body: The first Fable generation targeted sustained coding and knowledge work. Access was suspended June 12 and restored July 1; Fable 5.1 is now the newer release. The original launch promotion is not a current subscription allowance.
cards.gap: Track revised access, prices, independent evaluations, completed-task costs and reliability.

cards.title: Claude Fable 5.1
cards.body: Targets long-running coding, knowledge work and research. Cache reads cost $0.25 per million tokens. Anthropic estimates workload-dependent savings versus Fable 5; those are not guaranteed savings on every task. Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise access is documented, subject to plan limits.
cards.gap: Track revised access, prices, independent evaluations, completed-task costs and reliability.

cards.title: GPT-6 Astra
cards.body: OpenAI documents text/image input, text output, a 1,050,000-token context window and 128,000 maximum output tokens. Intended for reasoning, coding, computer use, research and documents. Client and account access varies with rollout. Cached input is $1 per million tokens; long contexts and Fast mode cost more.
cards.gap: Track revised access, prices, independent evaluations, completed-task costs and reliability.

cards.title: Grok 4.6
cards.body: Targets coding, agentic tasks and knowledge work. The API documents text/image input, text output and a 500,000-token context window. Cached input costs $0.50 per million tokens. Requests beyond 200K context use higher pricing. Released in Grok Build and Cursor; API details are separately documented.
cards.gap: Track revised access, prices, independent evaluations, completed-task costs and reliability.

cards.title: Claude Mythos 5.1
cards.body: Anthropic describes the same underlying model as Fable 5.1 with different safeguards, available through vetted access programs. A higher consumer subscription does not establish Mythos access.
cards.gap: Track revised access, prices, independent evaluations, completed-task costs and reliability.

cards.title: Grok Bot
cards.stage: Agent product · available with eligible plans
cards.body: Persistent agents work on their own computers across connected apps and scheduled tasks. This is an agent product, not a new base model or proof of autonomous productivity. The August 26 announcement expands access across SuperGrok and Cursor plans and describes a separate Bot usage allowance. Account terms should be checked at signup.
cards.gap: Track revised access, prices, independent evaluations, completed-task costs and reliability.

cards.title: Grok 4.7
cards.body: A requested successor to track. This review did not find a released 4.7 model entry in the accessible first-party documentation. The reported founder timing post could not be retrieved, so no launch date, API price, context length or benchmark score is published here.
cards.gap: Verify the original timing announcement, then a dated release note, documented model ID, pricing, access and model card. A forecast date passing is not a launch.

sections.title: AlphaFold: a Nobel-recognized advance for medicine.
sections.intro: Knowing a protein’s shape helps researchers investigate how it works and where a drug might bind. AlphaFold makes predicted structures available early in discovery, helping scientists choose what to test. The benefit is a better starting point for experiments—not an automatic route to an approved treatment.

cards.title: The 2024 Nobel recognition
cards.body: Demis Hassabis and John Jumper jointly received half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for protein structure prediction, following their work on AlphaFold2. David Baker received the other half for computational protein design. AlphaFold is a scientific application of AI beyond language and coding.
cards.gap: Keep AlphaFold2’s Nobel-recognized contribution distinct from subsequent models and from Baker’s protein-design work.

cards.title: More than 200 million predicted structures
cards.body: The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, developed by Google DeepMind and EMBL-EBI, provides open access to more than 200 million protein structure predictions. Researchers can begin with a structural hypothesis rather than starting every investigation without one. This is research infrastructure at scale, not a count of medicines discovered.
cards.gap: Track experimentally supported uses and task-specific time savings. Confidence varies by region and protein; predictions are not interchangeable with experimentally determined structures.

cards.title: 60% hit rate in a targeted discovery study
cards.body: Researchers screened over 16 million compounds computationally against TAAR1, a receptor of interest in neuropsychiatric research. Of 30 AlphaFold-selected candidates tested experimentally, 60% were hits—more than twice the homology-model comparator’s hit rate. A selected agonist also showed effects in mice. This demonstrates useful candidate selection in a specific preclinical workflow.
cards.gap: This is not a clinical success rate or evidence that total development time was halved. Track replication, optimization, toxicity and human trials separately; the study does not establish patient benefit.

cards.title: AlphaFold 3: predicting molecular interactions
cards.body: AlphaFold 3 extends prediction to complexes involving proteins, DNA, RNA, small molecules and other components. That can help researchers form hypotheses about binding and molecular interactions relevant to drug discovery. Structural prediction supports experiments; it does not alone establish binding strength, efficacy or safety.
cards.gap: Follow prospective experimental validation and measured improvements to discovery workflows. Keep model accuracy, discovery speed, trial outcomes and approved medicines as separate evidence.

sections.title: Open models widen who can build AI.
sections.intro: Open model developers, research institutes and community maintainers are central to the stack. Downloadable weights enable local deployment and adaptation; shared code, data and recipes can make research reproducible. These are different levels of openness, with different licenses and practical requirements.

cards.title: Ai2: opening the training process
cards.body: Ai2 publishes Olmo, Molmo and Tulu work with training code, data, weights and recipes. That gives researchers material to investigate model behavior and develop new methods, beyond simply querying a hosted API.
cards.gap: Check the specific release and its artifacts; openness does not establish reliability for every application.

cards.title: Mistral: reusable language and multimodal models
cards.body: Mistral publishes open-weight models alongside other commercial offerings. Its model catalog identifies Apache 2.0 releases including Mistral Small 4 and Mistral Large 3, while other entries have different terms. The contribution is a range of models developers can adapt and deploy.
cards.gap: License and access belong to a named checkpoint, not to the company as a whole.

cards.title: DeepSeek and Qwen: downloadable model families
cards.body: DeepSeek and Alibaba Qwen contribute models that developers can inspect, adapt and serve on their own infrastructure. DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3-32B provide concrete license references already tracked here. Derived models can retain obligations from their upstream base.
cards.gap: Do not apply one release’s license to every model in a family; downloads are not production deployments.

cards.title: Hugging Face: shared tools and a place to collaborate
cards.body: The Hub hosts versioned model and dataset repositories, model cards and Spaces applications. It helps independent developers, universities and companies share and build on each other’s work. Hosting a model does not make Hugging Face its original developer.
cards.gap: Public availability does not imply an unrestricted license. Repository counts and downloads do not establish business adoption.

cards.title: Hugging Face also builds models
cards.body: Hugging Face’s Smol Models research team develops SmolLM. The SmolLM3-3B card lists Apache 2.0 and publishes training details, including the data mixture and configurations. Smaller models offer a path to experimentation and deployment on more constrained hardware.
cards.gap: Measure memory, latency, quality and operating cost on the actual task; small size alone does not prove suitability.

cards.title: A wider community of builders
cards.body: The contributor directory also covers Meta, IBM, NVIDIA, Cohere, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Z.ai. Their model families and release policies differ. Community fine-tuners, dataset curators, evaluation authors and inference maintainers contribute alongside the original model developers.
cards.gap: Continue checkpoint-level coverage rather than labeling every product from these organizations open source.

sections.title: Omniverse and Cosmos: building AI for the physical world.
sections.intro: Physical AI needs environments in which to learn and test. Simulation and world models connect compute to robot development, autonomous systems and industrial workflows. NVIDIA supplies both, with distinct roles.

cards.title: Omniverse: simulation and industrial digital twins
cards.body: NVIDIA Omniverse provides libraries and technologies for OpenUSD-based physical AI applications, simulation and digital twins. Developers can represent facilities and equipment, connect engineering workflows and test scenarios virtually before applying changes in the real world.
cards.gap: OpenUSD interoperability does not make every Omniverse component open source. NVIDIA software terms apply; a digital twin is not evidence that a factory has been commissioned.

cards.title: Cosmos: world models for physical AI
cards.body: NVIDIA’s Cosmos world models support understanding and generation of physical-world scenarios. The Cosmos 3 research report describes omnimodal models and releases of code, checkpoints, synthetic datasets and evaluation resources. These models can support embodied-agent development beyond text-only LLM workflows.
cards.gap: Research benchmarks and generated scenes do not establish real-world robot safety or deployment. Check the exact model license; terms can differ between Cosmos generations.

cards.title: From a virtual scene to a tested machine
cards.body: An illustrative workflow combines a structured simulated environment, generated scenario variation, model training and evaluation, then controlled real-world testing. Omniverse and Cosmos supply complementary development tools. The useful outcome to track is better performance on a defined physical task.
cards.gap: This is a conceptual workflow, not a measured universal speedup. Track simulation-to-real transfer, failure rates, human intervention and verified operating deployments.

sections.title: Human expertise is part of the AI supply chain.
sections.intro: Official recruitment listings show tasks companies want people to perform. These micro1 examples connect human feedback to model development and robotics. They are advertised opportunities, not a count of completed hires or guaranteed earnings.

cards.title: Generalist: evaluate and annotate AI training data
cards.body: micro1 advertises remote contractor work at $50-$90 per hour. Tasks include evaluating and annotating datasets, reviewing model outputs and providing written feedback. The listing says prior AI experience is not required and emphasizes English communication, critical thinking and attention to detail.
cards.gap: The listing does not establish guaranteed paid hours, actual earnings, country-by-country eligibility or completed hires. Its scope is general AI training, not explicitly robotics.

cards.title: Video Annotation Specialist: teach through robot-task review
cards.body: micro1 advertises remote contractor work at $50-$90 per hour reviewing videos of robotic arms performing tasks. Contributors identify actions and outcomes, apply grading guidelines and produce structured annotations. Video annotation experience is preferred; AI training or robotics experience is strongly preferred.
cards.gap: Advertised rates are not verified pay received. Neither this listing nor the Generalist listing states a 10,000-person hiring target or guaranteed hours. Track active paid contributors and accepted work separately.

cards.title: What would turn recruitment into an employment outcome?
cards.body: Follow these exact posting IDs through changes and closure, then seek disclosed active contributors, approved paid hours, compensation received and project duration. Keep the two roles separate and avoid counting reposts as additional positions. The first-party listings verify tasks and advertised rates; they do not measure economy-wide job creation.
cards.gap: Publication dates were not disclosed. Pages were read manually in a public browser without logging in; the current HTML-only research runner may still fail to read their JavaScript-rendered content.
